headline: Contracts signed. Budgets increased. Startups funded.
deck: This week saw significant contracts awarded and funding rounds closed, underscoring the financial undercurrents in the space sector.

stories.head: Northrop Grumman bags $398M Space Force deal
stories.body: The Space Force awarded Northrop Grumman a $398 million contract for a new communications satellite, reinforcing the notion that in the space industry, contracts are often more about political connections than technical prowess. This deal highlights the ongoing trend of military spending in space as the U.S. looks to bolster its strategic capabilities.
stories.soWhat: For Northrop, this is a hefty win, but it also raises questions about the sustainability of such contracts when the competition is heating up.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amidst defense pull
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The focus on co-orbital security and space domain awareness (SDA) is timely, given the heightened interest in national security applications in space. This round illustrates how defense needs are driving investment in innovative space solutions.
stories.soWhat: With defense pulling through, True Anomaly is positioning itself well, but the real challenge will be delivering on expectations in a crowded field.

stories.head: SpaceX sends 3,000 kg to ISS with CRS-34
stories.body: SpaceX successfully launched its CRS-34 cargo mission to the ISS, delivering nearly 3,000 kilograms of supplies. This mission is part of NASA's ongoing partnership with SpaceX, which has now become a regular occurrence. The launch reflects SpaceX's operational reliability and its critical role in supporting the ISS.
stories.soWhat: While this is just another day at the office for SpaceX, it underscores how dependent NASA has become on commercial partners for routine operations.

watchlist.title: Watch for ESA-China SMILE launch
watchlist.body: The upcoming ESA-China SMILE mission could set a precedent for future international collaborations in space research.

watchlist.title: Virgin Galactic's commercial service timeline
watchlist.body: If Virgin Galactic actually begins commercial service this year, we might finally see if the space tourism market is viable.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris tactical SDA bid
watchlist.body: Their collaboration could signal a shift in how tactical space capabilities are developed and deployed.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: With a $480 million extension, Palantir's role in defense remains critical, but it will be interesting to see how they manage the increased scrutiny.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
